argument:
IOI Properties' CFO rose from RM1.060bn to RM2.391bn, and cash after specified property/land/PP&E outlays but before acquisitions and interest was RM1.780bn. That operating improvement creates a plausible purchase scenario in which the expanded asset base supplies recurring rent, collections and earnings. Growing revenue provides a foundation beyond the annual profit-doubling headline.

Net debt of RM21.818bn before leases and borrowings growth of about 29.4% make this speculative. Fair-value and JV remeasurement gains contributed 51.31% of PBT, so 8.54x trailing earnings cannot establish cheapness; estimated forward P/E is 17.71x. Acquisitions and deposits exceeded the operating investment surplus and required net drawdowns. Better CFO makes successful conversion conceivable, not self-funding proven. The downtrend supplies no timing confirmation; buying requires recurring asset returns to catch up with financing commitments.
key_points: Improved CFO and pre-acquisition investment surplus anchor the operating scenario.
Noncash gains invalidate a simple low-trailing-P/E bargain claim.
Heavy net debt and acquisition funding make returns conditional on asset conversion.
